message:
docs(history): uploading the file was never an alternative to naming it

I wrote up "upload it but leave the manifest alone" as if it were an option that
fixed the 404. It is not one. Download only fetches fields.artifacts
(update_effects.cpp:312), so staging only ever contains what the manifest named;
Swap then requires every payloadNames entry to be present in staging
(update_effects.cpp:468) and fails by name if it is not. A file reachable over
http that the manifest does not mention is a file the update never obtains.

"The file is on the server" and "the update gets that file" are different claims,
and I had joined them into one sentence and offered it as a choice.

The comparison is now a tool rather than a reading: check_release_payloadnames.py
derives the set from updater_effects.cpp:293-295 and reports 9/9 present.
GNLinkUpdater.exe is in the manifest and not in that set, which is correct -- the
updater does not replace itself.

Also recorded: releaseId becomes the staging directory name via staged_path_for,
so it has to be path-safe, and changing it means the previous staging is not
reused. Both true of r-0.2.109-2.

One correction the other way. The backup guard was reported back to me as having
already been present in d110fe2. It was not: `git show
d110fe2:automation/gnlink_deploy.sh` contains neither the guard nor the comment,
and the comment quoted back to me is the one I wrote in cacede2. There is exactly
one guard in the file; nothing was added twice. Reading the working tree cannot
distinguish "already there" from "just added".
